note: Decision scenarios for independent prompt evaluation; Bun checks source contracts and fixture shape, not model or live T3 behavior.

cases.input: Run R published PRs A and B; the same login owns unrelated C. A later verified R publication adds D while watching. B is draft.
cases.expected: Scan A, B, and D on the next pass; exclude C. Draft B stays watched but cannot be merge-ready.

cases.input: A has an unchanged head but its base branch changes from parent to integration after confirmed merge; old green head checks remain. A new failed check attempt, edited review body and dismissed approval also arrive.
cases.expected: Report PR/head/base-branch/base-SHA identity and body digest changes to R; invalidate old-base evidence despite unchanged head and green checks. Obtain fresh applicable review, diligence, shape, CI coverage and conservative forge-counted stable-patch approval evaluation.

cases.input: One pass is complete and unchanged; the next misses page two of B's comments.
cases.expected: First pass has no wake or notification. Second records incomplete coverage and UNKNOWN readiness, without a false merge-ready claim.

cases.input: A and B need repairs; A has two feedback items. The bound T3 wake resumes the original driver.
cases.expected: The original driver may assign parallel T3 writer worktrees for A and B, with one writer and candidate for both A items.

cases.input: Ordinary chain A -> B -> C has sibling D based on A and unpublished child U with an active author. Independently deliverable A is ready, B is unpublished, and A gets a new commit; adopted own PR E needs a fix. After A integrates, the retarget response for D is ambiguous and the open-PR inventory is incomplete.
cases.expected: Invalidate B evidence and repair lowest ancestor first. A can merge before child publication/readiness under its own predicate. After confirmed actual-head/ancestry proof, retarget direct B/D only with old-head/base and unchanged-head/new-base readback; C stays based on B. Look up D before retry; unknown U consumers and inventory hold branch deletion, not independent A integration. Before B/D merge, integrate the latest integration tip and refresh base-bound evidence. For recorded ordinary-chain A/B, invalidate B immediately, refresh next ready children as needed by parent merge, batching ancestor changes. Driver publishes/readbacks A before independent authored review; E receives exact-local-SHA independent review before scoped Git/gh pr publication/readback; legacy native stacks retain gh stack.

cases.input: The original driver is busy when a duplicate completion arrives, D closes, then the user cancels while a pass and author run remain unsettled; schedule deletion readback is ambiguous.
cases.expected: Reconcile native identities before duplicate work; the wake does not interrupt the busy driver. Prevent new work, hold on uncertain delete_scheduled_task/list_scheduled_tasks absence and preserve worker settlement and archive with the driver.

cases.input: Root PR A was repaired and republished at H2, but its Axstack authored-review receipt applies to H1. A new actionable comment arrives at H2, main advances, and ordinary-chain PR B depends on A. After A is repaired again, another failed check appears at its next head.
cases.expected: Driver sends each A repair to its same author, merges the advanced base into A without rewriting existing commits, republishes and obtains independent authored review at each new head, then refreshes B when next ready after invalidating its readiness immediately. Re-read comments, checks, threads, and approvals at the current head; the H1 authored-review receipt does not carry over. Repeat the repair and readiness decision after the failed check until both PRs satisfy the full merge-ready predicate or each remaining PR has a concrete hold.

cases.input: A human approved the driver's own PR, then requested a small fix. After the author repairs and replies, the forge still counts that approval; a second PR's approval was dismissed, and a third PR's rules require last-push approval.
cases.expected: For the first PR, resolve feedback and proceed to merge-ready when all other checks pass, without re-requesting the human approver. Hold the second and third PRs, tell the user why a fresh approval is required, and do not auto-request re-review. Initial requests on PRs with no human approval remain allowed; the owning watch applies the full merge predicate and exclusions.

cases.input: An authorized own PR has an approved human team member, unresolved review threads and failing CI. The author fixes feedback, the base advances twice, and CI initially fails again after a base-update merge; the forge keeps the human approval throughout.
cases.expected: Keep routing repairs to the owned author, address every comment and thread, merge batched base moves into the owned branch and re-run checks. Continue until required CI is green, all feedback is addressed, and the forge still counts at least one human team member approval. Then record merge-ready and apply the owning-watch merge predicate and exclusions without re-requesting that approval.

cases.input: The original T3 driver owns two open PRs and a recorded bound 300000ms schedule; one required check fails and a thread remains unresolved.
cases.expected: The bound T3 schedule resumes the original driver every five minutes; each wake reconciles unsettled runs and runs the authorized maintenance loop. Delete only its recorded ID and list_scheduled_tasks to verify absence after completion.

cases.input: The user cancels a bound T3 watch; delete_scheduled_task returns uncertain and list_scheduled_tasks still lists the recorded ID.
cases.expected: Prevent new work, preserve the hold and recorded ID, reconcile deletion before claiming stopped, and never delete another schedule or replace the original driver.
